assumptions: All probabilities are synthetic and are not measured Sceye, AALTO, UAVOS or Luminous fleet reliability data.

The 30-day window labels the intended service interval, but the static Bernoulli model does not represent time-varying failures, repair distributions, maintenance schedules, launch/recovery or weather persistence.
Each node has 0.92 independent availability conditional on no active common-cause event; these independent node states are mutually independent.
One shared weather-grounding event occurs with probability 0.06 and simultaneously makes all three nodes unavailable.
One shared regional gateway dependency is available with probability 0.97 and is required for the service to count as available.
Common-cause weather and gateway dependency states are independent of one another and of independent node availability in this synthetic example.
The service is available when at least two HAPS are operational and the required shared gateway is available.
The single-node baseline uses haps-a with the same independent availability, weather event and shared gateway dependency.
The naive independent k-of-n comparator applies the same 0.92 per-node availability, k=2 threshold and 0.97 gateway availability but incorrectly omits the common-cause weather-grounding event.
Exact enumeration covers 2^3 independent node states × 2 weather states × 2 gateway states = 32 mutually exclusive scenarios.

The fleet k-of-n result is a service-availability probability for this synthetic model. It is not a measured fleet SLA, 30-day uptime observation, certified safety/reliability metric or operational availability forecast.
The 99.9% target is a synthetic design target only; this fixture's 89.52% service availability is deliberately below it and must not be presented as meeting the target.
